name: Immunodeficiency by Defective Expression of MHC Class I

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for MHC Class I Deficiency

criteria.description: Demonstrated reduced or absent expression of MHC class I molecules on peripheral blood lymphocytes by flow cytometry
History of recurrent severe respiratory tract infections including pneumonia and bronchitis
Identification of pathogenic mutations in genes involved in MHC class I antigen processing and presentation (e.g., TAP1, TAP2, TAPBP)
Normal serum immunoglobulin levels and normal T-cell counts
Lack of autoimmune manifestations differentiating from other immunodeficiencies

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of reduced or absent MHC class I expression on lymphocytes plus recurrent severe respiratory infections and identification of pathogenic mutations in MHC class I pathway genes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other immunodeficiencies and confirmation by genetic testing.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absent or markedly reduced MHC class I surface expression on lymphocytes
searchTerms: very low MHC class I on immune cells
lack of MHC I on lymphocytes
chronic lung disease with airway damage
persistent lung infection with airway widening

common.notes: Poor growth secondary to chronic illness
searchTerms: failure to gain weight as baby

occasional.notes: Bacterial skin infections secondary to immune dysfunction
Enlarged lymph nodes due to chronic infection

rare.symptomName: Neurological complications secondary to chronic hypoxia
rare.notes: Rare but possible in advanced disease
searchTerms: nerve problems due to low oxygen
brain and nerve damage from poor oxygen

laboratory: Absent or markedly reduced MHC class I expression on peripheral blood lymphocytes by flow cytometry
imaging: Chest X-ray or CT showing bronchiectasis and chronic lung changes
other: Poor response to standard antibiotic therapy due to immune defect
Absence of autoantibodies typical of other immunodeficiencies

distinguishingFeatures: Defective MHC class II expression instead of class I
More profound CD4+ T cell deficiency
Later onset and broader infection spectrum

redFlags: Severe recurrent bacterial respiratory infections in infancy
Markedly reduced or absent MHC class I expression on lymphocytes
Poor response to conventional antibiotic therapy
references: Alvarez-Errico D, et al. Bare lymphocyte syndrome type I: clinical and molecular features. J Clin Immunol. 2018.
